components.css: .ds-nav-shell { display:grid; grid-template-columns:210px minmax(0,1fr) auto; align-items:center; min-height:86px; padding:0 26px 0 30px; border:1px solid #e4e9e7; border-radius:15px; background:rgb(255 255 255 / 96%); color:#122238; box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgb(20 37 42 / 8%); font-family:Manrope,sans-serif; } .ds-nav-identity { display:grid; gap:2px; padding-right:24px; border-right:1px solid #e1e6e8; } .ds-nav-identity span { color:#5e6c74; font-size:11px; font-weight:700; letter-spacing:.12em; text-transform:uppercase; } .ds-nav-identity strong { font-size:17px; font-weight:800; } .ds-nav { display:flex; gap:7px; padding-left:26px; } .ds-nav button, .ds-nav-signout { min-height:50px; padding:9px 17px; border:0; border-radius:11px; background:transparent; color:#314a6b; font:600 15px Manrope,sans-serif; cursor:pointer; transition:background .18s ease,color .18s ease,transform .18s ease; } .ds-nav button[aria-current='page'] { background:#eaf7f2; color:#0e524b; font-weight:800; } .ds-nav button:not([aria-current='page']):hover, .ds-nav-signout:hover { background:#f0f7f5; color:#0e524b; transform:translateY(-1px); } .ds-nav button:focus-visible, .ds-nav-signout:focus-visible { outline:3px solid #0b8a69; outline-offset:3px; } .ds-nav-signout { min-height:42px; margin-left:16px; border:1px solid #cbd9dd; border-radius:6px; color:#0b504b; font-weight:800; white-space:nowrap; } @media (max-width:1000px) { .ds-nav-shell { grid-template-columns:1fr auto; gap:8px; padding-block:12px; } .ds-nav-identity { border-right:0; } .ds-nav { grid-column:1 / -1; grid-row:2; display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(6,minmax(0,1fr)); padding:7px 0 0; border-top:1px solid #e5ebed; } .ds-nav-signout { grid-column:2; grid-row:1; } } @media (max-width:700px) { .ds-nav { grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr)); } .ds-nav button { min-height:52px; padding-inline:8px; font-size:11px; } }

narrative.overview:
The authenticated Growth OS workspace follows the supplied product references. It uses a warm white canvas, quiet mint organic shapes, navy hierarchy, deep-green actions, white rounded panels, and small icon-led cues. The result is an Operate interface for scanning customer records, preparing reviewed follow-ups, handling reviews, reading stored results, and managing business settings.

The workspace should feel composed rather than sparse. Each page starts with one large title and a short description, then moves directly into the primary task. Tables, split work areas, metric cards, and settings groups follow the fixed reference compositions. Soft shadows separate work areas without making every row float.
keyCharacteristics: Warm white canvas with restrained mint curves, dots, and leaf detail at the edges.
Navy headings and copy with deep-green primary actions.
White panels with 15px corners and low-contrast neutral shadows.
Pale icon wells, status pills, and line icons that support scanning.
A white navigation capsule that keeps all six destinations visible.

rules.name: The Auth Boundary Rule
rules.body: The auth page keeps its larger marketing headline, 542px form card, and page-specific decorative composition. Do not copy that exact layout into signed-in work screens.

rules.name: The Green Action Rule
rules.body: Use deep green for the next useful action, active location, or positive stored value. Do not spread it across neutral reading content.

rules.name: The Semantic Status Rule
rules.body: Keep amber, red, blue, violet, and green status colors attached to text labels. Color never replaces the state name.

rules.name: The Single Page Title Rule
rules.body: Each work screen gets one large title. Use panel titles, labels, and metadata for every level beneath it.

rules.name: The Dense Copy Rule
rules.body: Keep descriptions short and factual. The visual system creates room for work, not promotional copy inside the app.

rules.name: The Reference Composition Rule
rules.body: Keep each page's implemented grid and content order. The supplied screenshots are the composition authority for Customers, Campaigns, Reviews, Results, and Settings.

rules.name: The Phone Task Order Rule
rules.body: When a split collapses, put the current record or result before secondary creation and import tools.

rules.name: The Soft Separation Rule
rules.body: Use low-opacity shadows on navigation, bounded panels, metrics, and dialogs. Table rows and text groups rely on borders and spacing.

rules.name: The Quiet Backdrop Rule
rules.body: Organic shapes and the leaf plate remain peripheral. Do not place detailed imagery under controls or records.

rules.name: The Rounded Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Match radius to component scale. Do not apply one large radius to every object.

rules.name: The Pill Meaning Rule
rules.body: Use full pills for lifecycle, eligibility, campaign state, review state, and small identity badges. Do not turn ordinary buttons or panels into capsules.

rules.name: The Visible State Rule
rules.body: Selected, active, pending, success, warning, and destructive states need text plus a visible fill, border, or control change.

rules.name: The Reviewed Action Rule
rules.body: Primary actions identify the next user-reviewed step. Secondary and quiet actions hold exports, alternate paths, reopen actions, and manual status marks.

dos: Do keep the warm white, mint, navy, and green palette consistent across every signed-in page.
Do preserve the reference-led page compositions and the complete six-destination navigation.
Do use white rounded panels and soft shadows for bounded work areas, not every record row.
Do pair status color with a written state and keep product claims tied to stored data.
Do preserve the 47px workspace control height, visible focus treatment, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do keep the public auth composition and its Demo labels scoped to the auth flow.
donts: Don't restore the old dark square register treatment inside the authenticated workspace.
Don't place organic imagery, dots, or mint curves under dense text, fields, charts, or table values.
Don't hide phone destinations behind a menu when the two-row grid fits.
Don't turn every row into a floating card or every control into a pill.
Don't use red, amber, blue, or violet without a named state or subject role.
Don't present the auth page's illustrative metrics as verified outcomes.
